about: Bird (Bird Global) is a Miami-based micro-mobility company that operated e-scooter and e-bike sharing across US and European cities. Founded in 2017 by Travis VanderZanden, it went public via SPAC in 2021 (NYSE: BRDS), and filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in December 2023; it was bought out by its Third Lane Mobility affiliate in 2024. Consumers rent via app. Familiar urban consumer brand through its scooters, now much smaller.

Sokon is a Chinese automotive manufacturer (Chongqing Sokon Industry Group, brand Seres, associated with the Seres-Huawei Aito partnership) that develops and manufactures automobiles, new energy vehicles and engines. Seres Group is listed in Shanghai and Hong Kong. The input lists funding of about 7.1 billion yuan. Consumer-facing through Aito vehicles in China, but little brand awareness abroad.

wiki.title: Seres Group
wiki.text: Seres Group (赛力斯集团股份有限公司) is a Chinese automotive manufacturer founded in September 1986 with headquarters in Chongqing, China. Born as a manufacturer of components for household appliances and shock absorbers, it currently produces electric cars, ICEs cars, motorcycles and commercial vehicles as well as shock absorbers and internal combustion engines. In 2022, the company renamed to Seres Group from Sokon Group. It operates through its subsidiaries Seres, Seres Hubei, XGJAO Motorcycle and Yu'an Shock Absorber Company.

about: ABB is a Zurich-based Swiss-Swedish multinational technology group in electrification, automation, motion and robotics, serving utilities, industry, transport and buildings in about 100 countries. Revenue is roughly $33 billion, with about 110,000 employees. It also runs the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship title sponsorship and EV charging (Terra chargers). Listed on SIX Swiss Exchange and Nasdaq Stockholm (ABBN). B2B, high business awareness and a notable sports sponsor.

wiki.title: ABB
wiki.text: ABB Group is a Swedish-Swiss technology company, that operates in the fields of electrification and automation. The company was formed in 1988 from the merger of two electrical engineering companies, ASEA of Sweden and Brown, Boveri & Cie (BBC) of Switzerland.

about: Europcar Mobility Group is a major European car and van rental company headquartered in Paris (Issy-les-Moulineaux), operating Europcar, Goldcar, InterRent and Ubeeqo in about 140 countries through company stations and franchises, with revenue near 3 billion euros. Founded 1949. It was taken private in 2023 by a consortium led by Attestor. Customers are leisure and business travellers. Strong consumer travel brand in Europe with sports and event partnerships.

Dana is a supplier of drivetrain and propulsion technology: axles, driveshafts, transmissions, e-motors, inverters and sealing and thermal-management products for light vehicles, commercial trucks, off-highway machinery and electric vehicles. Customers are vehicle manufacturers such as Ford, Stellantis and Cummins, with revenue of about $10 billion. Headquartered in Maumee, Ohio, with operations in about 30 countries. Listed on NYSE (DAN). In 2025 it agreed to sell its off-highway business to Allison Transmission. B2B supplier, little consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Dana (company)
wiki.text: Dana, proizvodnja in prodaja pijač is a major Slovenian manufacturer of alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages. It is located in the village of Mirna in southeastern Slovenia.

about: Urgently is a roadside assistance and vehicle services platform that connects drivers with a network of towing, jump-start, tyre-change and other service providers through a digital platform used by automakers, insurers and fleets. Customers are car brands, insurance companies and auto clubs, who offer the service to their drivers, and revenue is per-event and subscription based. Based in Vienna, Virginia. Crunchbase shows about $219 million in funding. Private. B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

TVS Holdings is a holding company of the TVS Group of Chennai, India, with interests in automotive components, motorcycles through TVS Motor Company, distribution and finance. Customers range from consumers to vehicle makers. Listed on the NSE and BSE. The Crunchbase funding figure is not meaningful. Part of one of India's best-known industrial families, with the TVS brand widely known.

Voyah is the premium electric vehicle brand of Dongfeng Motor Group, a Chinese state-owned automaker, selling the Free, Dreamer, Passion and Chaser models in China and abroad. It is sold in markets including Norway, where the Crunchbase entry places its European headquarters in Oslo, with exports across Europe, the Middle East and Southeast Asia. Customers are consumers and fleets buying plug-in hybrid and electric vehicles. Dongfeng restructured its listing in Hong Kong and moved Voyah toward a 2025 Hong Kong listing via a reverse takeover. Moderate consumer awareness in China, still building in Europe.

wiki.title: Voyah
wiki.text: Voyah is the luxury subsidiary of Chinese state-owned automaker Dongfeng Motor Corporation. Voyah was founded in April 2019, specializing in designing and developing premium electric vehicles. Dongfeng Motor Corporation unveiled its brand logo at the Big House Contemporary Art Center in Wuhan on 17 July 2020.

about: Swift Navigation is a San Francisco company that provides precise positioning (centimeter-level GNSS) software and hardware, including its Skylark service and Starling positioning engine, to automotive, autonomous vehicle and industrial customers. Founded in 2012. Crunchbase shows about $249 million in funding. B2B technology provider, known among automotive and robotics engineers.

Honeywell Aerospace makes aircraft engines (auxiliary power units, turbofans), avionics, cockpit systems, braking, satellites and parts and services for commercial, defence and space customers. Revenue near 15 billion dollars. Headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona. A segment of Honeywell, which has planned to spin it off as a separate listed company in the second half of 2026. B2B brand with low consumer awareness.

wiki.title: Honeywell Aerospace
wiki.text: Honeywell Aerospace Inc. is an independent American manufacturer of aircraft engines, avionics, auxiliary power units (APUs), navigation equipment, life-support and environmental control systems, hydraulics, flight data recorders, and other aviation and space systems. Headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, it operates as one of the world's largest standalone tier-1 aerospace and defense suppliers. The company generates approximately $15 billion in annual revenue from a balanced portfolio of commercial and military defense contracts.

about: United Launch Alliance (ULA) is a Centennial, Colorado-based rocket launch provider, a 50/50 joint venture of Boeing and Lockheed Martin formed in 2006, flying Atlas V, Delta IV and the new Vulcan Centaur rockets for NASA, the US Space Force, the National Reconnaissance Office, and commercial customers including Amazon's Project Kuiper. B2B and government, with high profile in the space industry and some public awareness from launch broadcasts.

AviLease is a Riyadh-based Saudi aircraft lessor owned by the Public Investment Fund, established in 2022, which buys and leases narrow- and wide-body aircraft to airlines and has placed large Airbus and Boeing orders. The input shows about $3.7 billion in funding. B2B aircraft leasing, with no consumer brand awareness.

about: Azul is a Sao Paulo-based Brazilian airline, founded in 2008 by David Neeleman, serving more than 150 destinations, mostly domestic, from its Campinas hub, with loyalty program TudoAzul. It carries about 30 million passengers a year and is listed on B3 and NYSE (AZUL). It filed for Chapter 11 in 2025. Consumers are Brazilian travellers. Strong consumer brand in Brazil, with football sponsorship.

Orbital Space Technology is a Beijing-based commercial aerospace company developing satellites and related space systems, including remote sensing small satellites and data services for commercial and government customers in China. The listed funding indicates significant private investment in China's commercial space sector. Operating status and revenue are not confirmed. B2B space company with low consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: StandardAero is a Scottsdale, Arizona aircraft engine maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) provider for business jets, helicopters, military and commercial aircraft, serving operators and engine makers like Honeywell, GE and Rolls-Royce. It has facilities across North America, Europe and Asia and about 7,000 employees, with revenue around 5 billion dollars. Owned by Carlyle until its NYSE listing (SARO) in October 2024. B2B aerospace services with limited public awareness.

Lyntia Networks is a Spanish neutral wholesale fibre-optic and telecom infrastructure operator based in Alcobendas, Madrid, offering dark fibre, backhaul and connectivity services to telecom operators. Customers are carriers and large network users. Crunchbase shows about $1.8 billion in funding, including infrastructure investor capital and debt. Private. B2B infrastructure brand, with no consumer awareness.

about: Yuanxin Satellite is a Shanghai-based provider of low-orbit broadband and multimedia satellite services in China, in the information and communications sector. The input shows funding of about 13.7 billion yuan. Likely state-linked B2B and government customers, with no consumer visibility. The input lists it in information and communications, but customer names, ownership and satellites are not given. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Phoenix Aviation Capital is a Stamford, Connecticut-based aircraft lessor, part of the Phoenix group, providing leased commercial aircraft and engines to airlines. Funding shown is about 2.4 billion dollars, probably credit facilities. B2B aviation finance with no consumer brand awareness.

about: CesiumAstro is an Austin, Texas company, founded in 2017, that builds active phased array communications payloads and terminals for satellites, aircraft and drones. It sells to defence, space and commercial customers and has raised about $965 million per the input, though public rounds were lower. B2B with limited awareness outside aerospace and defence.

Merit AirFinance is a New York based aviation finance firm arranging financing for aircraft, engines and upgrades, serving airlines and lessors. It provides structured financing and advisory rather than selling aircraft directly. Crunchbase shows about $817 million in funding. The input gives no further detail on its owners or size. It is a specialist B2B financial firm with low public brand awareness, though known within the aviation industry. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Global Jet Capital is a Danbury, Connecticut based aircraft finance company that provides leases and loans for business jets, serving corporate and private owners. It was established in 2014 and is backed by Carlyle and other investors, with one of the larger business aviation portfolios. Crunchbase shows funding of $659 million. It is a specialist B2B financial firm with brand recognition within the private aviation market, but not among the general public.

about: Soar Aviation is described by Crunchbase as an aviation company offering luxury air travel solutions, in the aerospace and air transport industries. It is based in Atlanta, Georgia, with about $1.03 billion in funding shown. Its customers are likely premium travellers, but ownership and fleet are not stated in the input. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: BOND is a Fort Lauderdale-based private aviation company, founded in 2015, offering a fractional jet and helicopter membership programme and aircraft management, with a concierge model. Wealthy individuals and corporate members buy shares in aircraft or flight time. It gained attention for its pre-pandemic Florida expansion. Crunchbase shows it raised around 440 million dollars. A premium consumer brand with niche awareness among business aviation customers.

about: SAS (Scandinavian Airlines) is a Stockholm-area airline group, based in Solna, and Scandinavia's largest airline, flying to over 120 destinations from Copenhagen, Oslo and Stockholm, with about 30 million passengers a year. It emerged from US Chapter 11 in 2024, with Air France-KLM taking a majority stake in 2025 alongside Apollo and Castlelake. SkyTeam member. A strong consumer brand across the Nordics, long a sports and event sponsor.

TrueNoord is a Dublin-based aircraft leasing and financing company focused on regional aircraft, providing financing solutions to airlines for turboprops and regional jets such as ATR, Embraer and De Havilland types. It was formed in 2018 by Noord Capital and has since expanded, with funding from asset managers and banks. It is a B2B lessor with low public visibility.

about: Mynaric is a Munich-based maker of laser communication terminals that link satellites to each other and to the ground, such as its CONDOR and HAWK products, for constellations in low earth orbit. Customers are satellite operators and defence organisations. Founded in 2009, it was listed on Nasdaq in 2021 and restructured in 2025 with its stock delisted. B2B with low consumer awareness.
